sections.name: Maternal-Fetal Physiology, Antenatal Screening, Pelvis and Fetal Surveillance

modules.name: Placenta, Fetal Development and Fetal Circulation

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 5 (Implantation and Placental Development), Ch 7 (Embryogenesis and Fetal Development)

mustKnow.fact: Trophoblast differentiates by day 6 to 7 post-fertilization into inner cytotrophoblast and outer syncytiotrophoblast, which invades maternal spiral arterioles converting them into high-flow low-resistance conduits.
Fetal circulation directs oxygenated blood from the umbilical vein via ductus venosus (bypassing liver) to inferior vena cava, then preferentially across foramen ovale into left atrium.
Ductus arteriosus shunts deoxygenated blood from the pulmonary artery into descending aorta, maintaining high pulmonary vascular resistance and low pulmonary perfusion in utero.
Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) peaks at 8 to 10 weeks of gestation at approximately 100,000 mIU/mL, produced by syncytiotrophoblast to rescue corpus luteum progesterone production.
Placental steroidogenesis lacks 17-alpha-hydroxylase and 17,20-desmolase, depending on fetal adrenal DHEA-S for 16-alpha-hydroxy-DHEA-S conversion into estriol.
Human placental lactogen (hPL) acts as maternal anti-insulin somatomammotropin, increasing lipolysis and maternal free fatty acids to spare glucose for transplacental gradient transfer.
Fetal hemoglobin (HbF) contains alpha-2 gamma-2 globin chains, conferring higher oxygen affinity and leftward shifted dissociation curve relative to adult HbA.
Single umbilical artery occurs in 0.5 to 1 percent of singleton births and is associated with chromosomal aneuploidy and renal-cardiac congenital anomalies.

modules.name: Maternal Physiological Changes in Pregnancy

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 4 (Maternal Physiology)

mustKnow.fact: Maternal cardiac output increases 40 to 50 percent above baseline by 20 to 24 weeks, driven initially by stroke volume expansion and later by increased resting heart rate.
Systemic vascular resistance falls due to nitric oxide and progesterone-mediated smooth muscle relaxation, with diastolic blood pressure nadir occurring at 24 to 28 weeks.
Plasma volume expands 45 to 50 percent while red cell mass increases only 20 to 30 percent, producing physiologic hemodilution with normal lowest hemoglobin at 10.5 g/dL in second trimester.
Renal blood flow and glomerular filtration rate (GFR) increase by 50 percent, lowering normal serum creatinine to 0.4 to 0.6 mg/dL; creatinine above 0.8 mg/dL indicates renal impairment.
Progesterone stimulates respiratory center drive, increasing minute ventilation by 40 percent via increased tidal volume, producing compensated respiratory alkalosis with PaCO2 28 to 32 mmHg.
Pregnancy induces hypercoagulability through increased factors I (fibrinogen), VII, VIII, IX, X, decreased protein S, and acquired activated protein C resistance.
Thyroxine-binding globulin doubles under estrogen stimulation, elevating total T3 and total T4 while free T3 and free T4 remain physiologically normal.

Gastroesophageal sphincter tone falls under progesterone influence and gastric emptying slows during active labour, heightening pulmonary aspiration risk (Mendelson syndrome) under general anaesthesia.

modules.name: Diagnosis of Pregnancy and Antenatal Care Schedules

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 8 (Preconceptional Care), Ch 9 (Prenatal Care)

mustKnow.fact: Transvaginal sonography visualizes gestational sac at 4.5 to 5 weeks with mean sac diameter of 2 to 3 mm, and yolk sac at 5.5 weeks when MSD reaches 8 to 10 mm.
Crown-rump length (CRL) measured between 7 and 13 weeks 6 days provides the most accurate dating of gestational age, with error margin of plus or minus 5 to 7 days.
Fetal heart pulsation must be demonstrated on transvaginal ultrasound once embryo crown-rump length measures 7 mm or more; lack of cardiac activity at 7 mm defines non-viable pregnancy.
Periconceptional folic acid supplementation at 400 micrograms daily prevents 70 percent of neural tube defects, whereas high-risk mothers require 4 to 5 mg daily starting 1 month preconception.
WHO 2016 antenatal care model recommends a minimum of 8 antenatal contacts: first contact before 12 weeks, subsequent visits at 20, 26, 30, 34, 36, 38, and 40 weeks.
Universal gestational diabetes screening with 75 g oral glucose tolerance test or DIPSI non-fasting single step is routinely performed between 24 and 28 weeks of gestation.
Group B Streptococcus (GBS) recto-vaginal screening culture is performed between 36 and 37 weeks 6 days, guiding intrapartum penicillin G prophylaxis.
Anti-D immunoglobulin is administered at 28 weeks of gestation to non-sensitized Rh-negative mothers (300 micrograms or 1500 IU) and within 72 hours of delivering an Rh-positive newborn.

modules.name: Prenatal Aneuploidy Screening and Invasive Diagnostic Procedures

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 13 (Genetics), Ch 14 (Prenatal Diagnosis)

mustKnow.fact: First trimester combined screening between 11 and 13 weeks 6 days evaluates nuchal translucency (NT), maternal serum free beta-hCG, and pregnancy-associated plasma protein A (PAPP-A), detecting 85 percent of trisomy 21.
Increased nuchal translucency thickness exceeding 3.5 mm or 99th percentile confers strong association with Down syndrome, Turner syndrome, and congenital cardiac structural anomalies.
Cell-free fetal DNA (cfDNA) non-invasive prenatal testing from maternal plasma from 10 weeks onwards achieves detection rate over 99 percent and false-positive rate under 0.1 percent for trisomy 21.

Second trimester quadruple marker screen between 15 and 20 weeks measures AFP, hCG, unconjugated estriol (uE3), and inhibin-A; trisomy 21 exhibits elevated hCG and inhibin-A with depressed AFP and uE3.

Elevated maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein (MSAFP) exceeding 2.5 multiples of the median (MoM) indicates open neural tube defects, abdominal wall defects (gastroschisis, omphalocele), or multiple gestations.

Chorionic villus sampling (CVS) is performed between 10 and 13 weeks transcervically or transabdominally, carrying pregnancy loss rate of 0.2 to 0.5 percent and limb reduction risk if done before 10 weeks.
Amniocentesis is performed under continuous ultrasound guidance from 15 weeks onward for fetal karyotyping, chromosomal microarray, and viral PCR, with procedure-related loss risk below 0.3 percent.
Confined placental mosaicism accounts for 1 to 2 percent of abnormal CVS karyotypes, requiring follow-up amniocentesis to evaluate true fetal lineage.

modules.name: Obstetric Pelvis, Diameters, Planes and Fetal Skull Landmarks

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 2 (Maternal Anatomy), Ch 22 (Normal Labor)

mustKnow.fact: Obstetric conjugate is the shortest anteroposterior diameter of pelvic inlet between sacral promontory and closest pubic symphysis point, measuring 10.5 cm, calculated as diagonal conjugate minus 1.5 to 2.0 cm.
Midpelvis transverse interspinous diameter between ischial spines measures 10.0 to 10.5 cm, representing the narrowest plane of the birth canal where station zero is defined.

Caldwell-Moloy classification categorizes female pelvis into gynecoid (round, 50 percent), android (heart-shaped, funnel, 25 percent), anthropoid (AP oval, 20 percent), and platypelloid (transverse oval, 5 percent).
Suboccipitobregmatic diameter is the presenting anteroposterior dimension in fully flexed vertex presentation, measuring 9.5 cm from below occipital protuberance to center of anterior fontanelle.
Occipitofrontal diameter measures 11.5 cm in deflexed (military) vertex presentation, extending from glabella to external occipital protuberance.
Mentovertical diameter measures 13.5 cm from chin to highest vertex point, representing the largest fetal head diameter presenting in brow presentation, typically precluding vaginal delivery.
Submentobregmatic diameter measures 9.5 cm from junction of chin and neck to anterior fontanelle, presenting in fully extended face presentation.
Biparietal diameter (BPD) is the greatest transverse diameter of fetal head between parietal eminences, averaging 9.5 cm at term.

modules.name: Disorders of Amniotic Fluid: Oligohydramnios, Polyhydramnios and Amnioinfusion

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 11 (Amnionic Fluid)

mustKnow.fact: Amniotic fluid volume peaks at approximately 800 to 1000 mL at 34 to 36 weeks of gestation, then declines to 400 to 600 mL at post-term gestations beyond 41 weeks.
From 16 weeks gestation onwards, fetal swallowing and fetal urination become the primary regulatory pathways for amniotic fluid production and turnover.
Oligohydramnios is sonographically defined by amniotic fluid index (AFI) 5 cm or less, or single deepest vertical pocket (DVP) under 2 cm.
Early severe oligohydramnios before 20 weeks gestation results in Potter sequence, featuring pulmonary hypoplasia, compressed facies, clubfoot, and skeletal limb contractures.
Polyhydramnios is defined as amniotic fluid index of 24 to 25 cm or greater, or single deepest vertical pocket measuring 8 cm or greater.
Etiology of polyhydramnios includes maternal diabetes mellitus, fetal gastrointestinal tract atresia (duodenal atresia, tracheoesophageal fistula), neural tube defects, and fetal hydrops.
Therapeutic amniocentesis (amnioreduction) is indicated in symptomatic polyhydramnios with maternal severe dyspnoea, draining at 1000 to 1500 mL per session under ultrasound guidance.
Intrapartum amnioinfusion of warm normal saline relieves repetitive variable fetal heart rate decelerations caused by umbilical cord compression in oligohydramnios.

modules.name: Teratology, Teratogens, Fetotoxic Drugs and Radiation Exposure

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 12 (Teratology, Teratogens, and Fetotoxic Agents)

mustKnow.fact: Classic embryonic period of organogenesis spans 3 to 8 post-conception weeks (gestational weeks 5 to 10), marking peak susceptibility to major structural teratogen-induced malformations.
Thalidomide produces severe phocomelia, amelia, and radial ray deficiencies when exposure occurs between gestational days 34 and 50.
Isotretinoin embryopathy includes microtia or anotia, micrognathia, conotruncal heart defects, hydrocephalus, and thymic hypoplasia, mandating strict pregnancy prevention programs.
Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers in second/third trimesters cause fetopathy with renal tubular dysgenesis, oligohydramnios, and neonatal anuria.
Warfarin exposure between 6 and 9 weeks gestation leads to fetal warfarin syndrome characterized by nasal hypoplasia, stippled epiphyses (chondrodysplasia punctata), and CNS abnormalities.
Sodium valproate confers 1 to 2 percent risk of lumbar open neural tube defects, craniofacial dysmorphism, cardiac defects, and dose-dependent long-term neurocognitive impairment.
Fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS) is characterized by prenatal and postnatal growth restriction, microcephaly, smooth philtrum, thin vermilion border, short palpebral fissures, and CNS dysfunction.
Diagnostic ionizing radiation below 50 mGy (5 rads) is not associated with increased risk of fetal anomalies, growth restriction, or miscarriage.

modules.name: Rh Alloimmunisation, Kell Antibodies and Fetal Hydrops

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 15 (Fetal Disorders), Ch 16 (Fetal Therapy)

mustKnow.fact: RhD alloimmunisation develops when an RhD-negative woman carries an RhD-positive fetus and experiences fetomaternal hemorrhage, producing anti-D IgG antibodies that cross placenta.
Critical anti-D antibody titer is conventionally 1:16 or 1:32, beyond which serial middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity (MCA-PSV) Doppler monitoring is mandatory.
Middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity (MCA-PSV) exceeding 1.5 multiples of the median (MoM) predicts moderate-to-severe fetal anaemia with sensitivity exceeding 95 percent.
mustKnow.source: Williams Obs 25e Ch 15; Mari et al NEJM

mustKnow.fact: Anti-Kell antibodies cause severe fetal anaemia predominantly through bone marrow suppression of erythroid progenitors rather than solely peripheral reticuloendothelial hemolysis.
Fetal hydrops is defined by pathologic fluid accumulation in two or more fetal compartments (ascites, pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, skin oedema) or one compartment plus polyhydramnios.

Intrauterine blood transfusion is performed via ultrasound-guided cordocentesis into umbilical vein using O-negative, irradiated, CMV-negative, leukoreduced packed red cells cross-matched against maternal serum.
Rosette test provides qualitative screening for fetomaternal hemorrhage exceeding 10 mL, while Kleihauer-Betke acid-elution test quantifies fetal cells to calculate extra anti-D vials.
Standard 300 microgram (1500 IU) dose of anti-D covers up to 30 mL of fetal whole blood or 15 mL of fetal packed red cells.

sections.name: Early Pregnancy Loss, Ectopic, GTD and Late Pregnancy Complications

modules.name: Miscarriage, Medical Termination of Pregnancy and MTP Act 2021

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 18 (Abortion); MTP (Amendment) Act 2021

mustKnow.fact: Threatened abortion presents with vaginal bleeding through a closed cervical os with viable intrauterine embryo, managed expectantly as two-thirds proceed to viable birth.
Inevitable abortion is marked by vaginal bleeding with open internal cervical os and ruptured membranes or cervical effacement, where progression to pregnancy expulsion is unavoidable.
Medical abortion up to 63 days (9 weeks) gestation uses mifepristone 200 mg orally followed 24 to 48 hours later by misoprostol 800 micrograms buccally, sublingually or vaginally.

Under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act 2021, termination up to 20 weeks requires opinion of one registered medical practitioner, and between 20 and 24 weeks requires opinion of two registered medical practitioners for specified vulnerable categories.
Termination beyond 24 weeks under MTP Act 2021 is permissible only upon diagnosis of substantial fetal abnormalities by a state-level four-member Medical Board.
Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) is defined as two or more failed clinical pregnancies, warranting workup for parental karyotyping, uterine cavity anomalies, and antiphospholipid antibodies.
Cervical insufficiency presents with painless painless second-trimester cervical dilatation and membrane prolapse, managed by elective cerclage (McDonald or Shirodkar) at 12 to 14 weeks.
Surgical evacuation of incomplete or septic abortion uses manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) or suction curettage under prophylactic doxycycline or broad-spectrum antibiotic coverage.

modules.name: Ectopic Pregnancy: Methotrexate Protocol, Salpingostomy and Ruptured Ectopic

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 19 (Ectopic Pregnancy)

mustKnow.fact: Over 95 percent of ectopic pregnancies implant within the fallopian tube, with the ampulla being the commonest site (70 percent), followed by isthmus (12 percent), and fimbria (11 percent).
Discriminatory zone is the serum beta-hCG level (1500 to 2000 mIU/mL on transvaginal sonography) above which a viable intrauterine gestational sac must be consistently visible.

Transvaginal ultrasound findings diagnostic of tubal ectopic pregnancy include an extrauterine sac with yolk sac or embryo ('tubal ring sign') and complex adnexal mass with vascular 'ring of fire' Doppler pattern.

Systemic single-dose methotrexate (50 mg/m2 BSA intramuscularly) is eligible when hemodynamically stable, unruptured mass under 3.5 cm, serum beta-hCG under 5000 mIU/mL, and absent embryonic cardiac activity.
Following single-dose methotrexate, serum beta-hCG is monitored on day 4 and day 7; a decline of 15 percent or more between day 4 and 7 indicates therapeutic response.
Interstitial (cornual) ectopic pregnancy implants in the myometrial segment of the tube, rupturing later at 12 to 16 weeks with catastrophic torrential haemorrhage from uterine artery anastomoses.

Laparoscopic salpingostomy preserves fertility in unruptured tubal pregnancy with desire for future childbearing, requiring post-procedure weekly hCG monitoring to exclude persistent trophoblastic tissue.
Ruptured ectopic pregnancy with hemoperitoneum, peritoneal signs, and hypovolemic shock mandates emergent volume resuscitation and emergency laparoscopic or open salpingectomy.

modules.name: Gestational Trophoblastic Disease, Hydatidiform Mole and FIGO WHO Scoring

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 20 (Gestational Trophoblastic Disease)

mustKnow.fact: Complete hydatidiform mole arises from fertilization of an enucleated ovum by a single sperm that duplicates (46,XX, 90 percent) or two sperm (46,XY), lacking fetal parts and demonstrating diffuse hydropic villous swelling.

Partial hydatidiform mole results from dispermic fertilization of a haploid ovum producing triploid karyotype (69,XXY, 69,XXX), featuring focal trophoblastic hyperplasia, identifiable fetal tissue, and scalloped villi.

Classic ultrasound appearance of complete mole is the 'snowstorm' or 'bunch of grapes' intra-amniotic echogenic pattern without fetus, often accompanied by bilateral theca lutein cysts exceeding 6 cm.
Primary treatment for hydatidiform mole is suction evacuation and curettage under oxytocin infusion, with anti-D administered to Rh-negative women.
Post-molar gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) is diagnosed if beta-hCG plateaus across 4 values over 3 weeks, rises across 3 values over 2 weeks, or persists elevated beyond 6 months.
FIGO-WHO prognostic scoring system stratifies GTN into low-risk (score 0 to 6) and high-risk (score 7 or greater) based on age, antecedent pregnancy, interval, hCG level, tumor size, and metastases.
Low-risk GTN (score 6 or less) is treated with single-agent chemotherapy (methotrexate with folinic acid rescue or pulsed dactinomycin), achieving cure rates approaching 100 percent.
High-risk GTN (score 7 or greater) or choriocarcinoma mandates multi-agent chemotherapy with the EMA-CO regimen (etoposide, methotrexate, dactinomycin, cyclophosphamide, vincristine).

modules.name: Preeclampsia, Eclampsia, HELLP Syndrome and Magnesium Sulphate Protocols

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 40 (Hypertensive Disorders); ACOG/ISSHP Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Preeclampsia is diagnosed after 20 weeks gestation by new-onset systolic BP 140 mmHg or greater or diastolic 90 mmHg or greater on two occasions 4 hours apart, plus proteinuria (>=300 mg/24h or PCR >=0.3).

Preeclampsia with severe features includes systolic BP >=160 mmHg or diastolic >=110 mmHg, platelets <100,000/microL, serum creatinine >1.1 mg/dL, elevated transaminases twice normal, pulmonary oedema, or cerebral-visual symptoms.
First-line antihypertensive therapy for acute severe hypertension (BP >=160/110 mmHg) includes intravenous labetalol, intravenous hydralazine, or oral immediate-release nifedipine.

Magnesium sulphate is the drug of choice for eclampsia prevention and seizure treatment, administered via Pritchard intramuscular regimen (4 g IV plus 10 g IM, then 5 g IM 4-hourly) or Zuspan intravenous regimen (4 to 6 g IV loading then 1 to 2 g/h).

Therapeutic serum magnesium level is 4.8 to 8.4 mg/dL (2.0 to 3.5 mmol/L); loss of patellar reflexes occurs at 9 to 12 mg/dL, respiratory depression at 12 to 15 mg/dL, and cardiac arrest above 15 mg/dL.
Calcium gluconate (10 mL of 10 percent solution IV over 3 minutes) is the immediate antidote for magnesium sulfate toxicity.
HELLP syndrome comprises microangiopathic Hemolysis (schistocytes, elevated LDH >600 U/L), Elevated Liver enzymes (AST/ALT >=70 U/L), and Low Platelets (<100,000/microL).

Definitive management is delivery: at 37 weeks for gestational hypertension or preeclampsia without severe features, and at 34 weeks (or immediately upon maternal-fetal decompensation) for preeclampsia with severe features.

modules.name: Antepartum Haemorrhage: Placenta Praevia, Abruptio Placentae and Vasa Praevia

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 41 (Obstetrical Hemorrhage)

mustKnow.fact: Placenta praevia presents characteristically with sudden, painless, causeless, recurrent bright red vaginal bleeding in the third trimester without uterine tenderness.
Digital vaginal examination is strictly contraindicated in unexplained third-trimester vaginal bleeding until ultrasound localization definitively excludes placenta praevia.
Low-lying placenta is defined when the placental edge lies within 20 mm (2 cm) of the internal os without covering it, whereas placenta praevia completely or partially overlaps the os.
Abruptio placentae presents with painful dark vaginal bleeding, uterine hypertonicity, woody-hard uterine tenderness, and fetal distress, with maternal hypertension being the leading risk factor.
Concealed retroplacental hemorrhage accounts for 20 percent of placental abruptions, where blood extravasates into myometrium producing a bruised, mottled Couvelaire uterus.

Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) involves direct trophoblastic attachment to myometrium without intervening decidua basalis (accreta), into myometrium (increta), or through serosa into bladder (percreta).
Vasa praevia occurs when unsupported fetal vessels within velamentous cord insertion or succenturiate lobe cross the internal os, presenting with fetal bradycardia and bleeding upon membrane rupture.
Apt test or Ogita test differentiates fetal hemoglobin (alkali-resistant, remains pink) from maternal adult hemoglobin (turns yellow-brown on adding 1 percent sodium hydroxide) in vasa praevia.

modules.name: Preterm Labour, Tocolysis, Antenatal Corticosteroids, PROM and Post-term

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 42 (Preterm Birth), Ch 43 (Postterm Pregnancy)

mustKnow.fact: Preterm labour is defined as regular uterine contractions with progressive cervical effacement or dilatation between 20 and 36 weeks 6 days of gestation.

Cervical length under 25 mm on transvaginal sonography between 16 and 24 weeks or negative fetal fibronectin (fFN <50 ng/mL) in cervicovaginal fluid provides high negative predictive value (>95%) for delivery within 7 to 14 days.

Antenatal corticosteroids (betamethasone 12 mg IM 24 hours apart x 2 doses, or dexamethasone 6 mg IM 12 hours apart x 4 doses) between 24 and 34 weeks significantly reduce neonatal respiratory distress syndrome, intraventricular hemorrhage, and neonatal death.
Magnesium sulphate administered before 32 weeks gestation provides fetal neuroprotection, reducing the risk of cerebral palsy and gross motor dysfunction in surviving infants.

First-line tocolytics (calcium channel blocker nifedipine or oxytocin receptor antagonist atosiban) are administered for up to 48 hours to enable complete corticosteroid course and in-utero maternal transport.
Preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) is confirmed by sterile speculum pooling, positive nitrazine test (pH >6.5 turns blue), and microscopic ferning arborization pattern.
Latency antibiotic regimen for PPROM remote from term (<34 weeks) combines intravenous ampicillin and erythromycin for 48 hours, followed by oral amoxicillin and erythromycin for 5 days.

Post-term pregnancy extends to or beyond 42 weeks 0 days, carrying elevated risks of meconium aspiration syndrome, macrosomia, and dysmaturity syndrome, with routine induction recommended between 41 and 42 weeks.

modules.name: Fetal Growth Restriction, Biophysical Profile and Umbilical Doppler

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 10 (Fetal Imaging), Ch 17 (Fetal Assessment), Ch 44 (Fetal-Growth Disorders)

mustKnow.fact: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is defined by estimated fetal weight (EFW) or abdominal circumference (AC) below the 10th percentile for gestational age, with severe FGR defined below the 3rd percentile.

Symmetrical FGR results from early intrinsic insults (chromosomal aneuploidies, congenital TORCH infections) with proportionally small head and body, whereas asymmetrical FGR arises from uteroplacental insufficiency with brain-sparing head sparing.

Umbilical artery Doppler measures placental vascular resistance; progression proceeds from increased systolic/diastolic (S/D) ratio and pulsatility index to absent end-diastolic flow (AEDF), and reversed end-diastolic flow (REDF).
Ductus venosus Doppler waveform reflects right atrial pressure; absent or reversed a-wave during atrial contraction indicates severe fetal acidemia and impending intrauterine demise.

Manning biophysical profile (BPP) evaluates 5 biophysical variables scored 0 or 2: non-stress test (NST), fetal breathing movements, gross body movements, fetal tone, and amniotic fluid volume (max score 10/10).
Modified biophysical profile combines non-stress test (reflecting acute acid-base status) and single deepest vertical pocket of amniotic fluid (reflecting chronic placental perfusion).
A reactive non-stress test (NST) in pregnancies >=32 weeks requires at least two accelerations of 15 bpm above baseline lasting 15 seconds (15x15 criteria) within a 20-minute window.
Delivery is indicated at 32 weeks for persistent reversed end-diastolic flow (REDF) and at 34 weeks for absent end-diastolic flow (AEDF) in umbilical artery after steroid administration.

modules.name: Multiple Pregnancy: Chorionicity, TTTS, TAPS, TRAP and Delivery Timing

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 45 (Multifetal Pregnancy)

mustKnow.fact: Chorionicity and amnionicity in monozygotic twins depend on cleavage timing: days 0 to 3 yields dichorionic diamniotic (30%), days 4 to 8 monochorionic diamniotic (70%), days 8 to 12 monochorionic monoamniotic (1-2%), and after day 13 conjoined twins.
First trimester ultrasound establishes chorionicity via lambda (twin peak) sign in dichorionic twins and T-sign in monochorionic twins with over 98 percent accuracy.
Twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS) occurs in 10 to 15 percent of monochorionic diamniotic pregnancies due to unbalanced deep arteriovenous placental anastomoses.

Quintero staging classifies TTTS from Stage I (polyhydramnios-oligohydramnios sequence, DVP >8 cm and <2 cm) through Stage II (empty donor bladder), Stage III (abnormal Dopplers), Stage IV (hydrops), to Stage V (fetal demise).
mustKnow.source: Williams Obs 25e Ch 45; Quintero et al

mustKnow.fact: Fetoscopic laser photocoagulation of communicating placental anastomoses between 16 and 26 weeks is the gold standard treatment for Quintero Stage II to IV TTTS.
Twin anaemia-polycythaemia sequence (TAPS) is characterized by large inter-twin hemoglobin difference (>5 g/dL) with discordant MCA-PSV without amniotic fluid discordance.

Twin reversed arterial perfusion (TRAP) sequence features a normal pump twin perfusing an acardiac acephalic twin via retrograde umbilical arterial flow, treated with radiofrequency ablation of acardiac cord.

Optimal timing of delivery without complications is 37 to 38 weeks for dichorionic diamniotic twins, 36 to 37 weeks for monochorionic diamniotic twins, and 32 to 34 weeks by elective cesarean for monochorionic monoamniotic twins.

modules.name: Anaemia in Pregnancy: Iron Deficiency, Megaloblastic and Haemoglobinopathies

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 56 (Hematological Disorders)

mustKnow.fact: WHO defines anaemia in pregnancy as hemoglobin below 11.0 g/dL in first and third trimesters, and below 10.5 g/dL in second trimester, with severe anaemia defined as hemoglobin under 7.0 g/dL.
Iron deficiency anaemia is the commonest cause (75 to 80 percent), diagnosed by serum ferritin below 30 micrograms/L, microcytic hypochromic indices, and elevated total iron binding capacity.
Total iron requirement during a singleton pregnancy is approximately 1000 mg (300 mg fetus/placenta, 500 mg maternal RBC expansion, 200 mg obligate gastrointestinal and skin losses).
Intravenous iron (ferric carboxymaltose or iron sucrose) calculated by Ganzoni formula is indicated for oral iron intolerance, severe second/third trimester anaemia, or malabsorption.
Megaloblastic anaemia in pregnancy is almost universally due to folic acid deficiency, featuring hypersegmented neutrophils on peripheral smear and macrocytic red cell indices.
Beta-thalassemia trait presents with mild microcytic anaemia and disproportionately normal or elevated red blood cell count, confirmed by HbA2 exceeding 3.5 percent on hemoglobin electrophoresis.
Sickle cell disease (HbSS) in pregnancy carries heightened risks of vaso-occlusive bone pain crises, acute chest syndrome, preeclampsia, and placental infarction.
Prophylactic blood transfusion is not routinely recommended in sickle cell pregnancy, but exchange transfusion is life-saving for acute chest syndrome, stroke, or refractory crisis.

modules.name: Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Screening, DIPSI, Glycaemic Targets and Insulin

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 57 (Diabetes Mellitus)

mustKnow.fact: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is carbohydrate intolerance of variable severity with onset or first recognition during pregnancy, driven by placental anti-insulin hormones including hPL, cortisol, and progesterone.
IADPSG and WHO 2013 diagnostic criteria utilize a 75 g 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test: fasting >=92 mg/dL, 1-hour >=180 mg/dL, or 2-hour >=153 mg/dL, with any single abnormal value diagnostic.
DIPSI criteria (single-step non-fasting 75 g glucose load) widely utilized in Indian public healthcare defines GDM when 2-hour venous plasma glucose reaches or exceeds 140 mg/dL.
mustKnow.source: DIPSI Guidelines India; Williams Obs 25e Ch 57

mustKnow.fact: Strict self-monitored blood glucose targets are fasting <95 mg/dL, 1-hour postprandial <140 mg/dL, and 2-hour postprandial <120 mg/dL to minimize fetal macrosomia and asymmetric septal hypertrophy.
Insulin is the preferred gold standard pharmacotherapy when medical nutrition therapy fails to achieve glycaemic targets within 1 to 2 weeks.
Metformin crosses the placenta freely but serves as an acceptable oral alternative in women unwilling or unable to administer insulin, though up to 40 percent require supplemental insulin.

Fetal complications of maternal diabetes include macrosomia (shoulder dystocia risk), neonatal hypoglycemia, polycythemia, hyperbilirubinemia, respiratory distress syndrome, and sacral agenesis (caudal regression).
Elective cesarean delivery is recommended in diabetic mothers when estimated fetal weight exceeds 4500 g to prevent severe shoulder dystocia and brachial plexus injury.

modules.name: Cardiac Disease in Pregnancy: WHO Risk Classes, Valve Lesions and Peripartum Cardiomyopathy

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 49 (Cardiovascular Disorders); ESC 2018 Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Modified WHO classification stratifies maternal cardiovascular risk from Class I (mild pulmonary stenosis, repaired ASD/VSD) to Class IV (maternal mortality 40 to 50%, pregnancy contraindicated).

Modified WHO Class IV conditions where pregnancy is absolute contraindication include severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, pulmonary arterial hypertension, Eisenmenger syndrome, and severe systemic LV dysfunction (LVEF <30%).

Severe mitral stenosis (mitral valve area <1.0 cm2) carries extreme risk of acute pulmonary oedema during labor, requiring beta-blocker rate control and percutaneous balloon mitral valvuloplasty if refractory.

Mechanical prosthetic heart valves in pregnancy mandate therapeutic anticoagulation throughout pregnancy, weighing warfarin embryopathy against valve thrombosis risk with low-molecular-weight heparin.
Warfarin at doses under 5 mg daily provides lowest valve thrombosis rates and low teratogenicity risk in first trimester, while dose-adjusted LMWH with anti-Xa monitoring is the alternative.
Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is idiopathic heart failure secondary to left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVEF <45%) presenting in the last month of pregnancy or first 5 months postpartum.
mustKnow.source: Williams Obs 25e Ch 49; Heart Failure Association

mustKnow.fact: PPCM pathogenesis involves 16-kDa cleaved prolactin fragment inducing endothelial damage, and bromocriptine therapy blocking prolactin release promotes myocardial recovery.
Vaginal delivery with early epidural analgesia and assisted second stage (forceps or vacuum) is preferred for most stable cardiac patients to avoid tachycardia and hemodynamic stress of pushing.

modules.name: Maternal and Perinatal Infections: TORCH, HIV, Hepatitis, Syphilis and Malaria

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 64 (Infectious Diseases), Ch 65 (Sexually Transmitted Infections)

mustKnow.fact: Congenital Toxoplasmosis features classic Sabin triad of chorioretinitis, intracranial calcifications, and hydrocephalus, treated maternally with spiramycin for prophylaxis or pyrimethamine-sulfadiazine for confirmed fetal infection.

Congenital Rubella Syndrome results from primary maternal infection in first 10 weeks gestation (up to 90% risk), manifesting classic triad of sensorineural deafness, cataract, and patent ductus arteriosus.
Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is the commonest congenital viral infection, leading cause of non-hereditary sensorineural hearing loss and periventricular calcifications with microcephaly.

Congenital syphilis presents with snuffles, hepatosplenomegaly, osteochondritis (Wimberger sign), and later Hutchinson teeth and mulberry molars, effectively prevented by maternal benzathine penicillin G.

Mother-to-child transmission of HIV is reduced below 1 to 2 percent with combination antiretroviral therapy (cART), avoidance of breastfeeding, and elective cesarean section if viral load exceeds 1000 copies/mL.

Hepatitis B vertical transmission reaches 90 percent in HBeAg-positive mothers; administration of hepatitis B immunoglobulin (HBIG) and hepatitis B vaccine within 12 hours of birth reduces transmission below 5 percent.
Maternal tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) therapy from 28 to 32 weeks is recommended for chronic hepatitis B mothers with high viral loads exceeding 200,000 IU/mL.

Falciparum malaria in pregnancy sequesters within placental intervillous spaces producing severe maternal anaemia, low birth weight, and preterm birth, prevented by intermittent preventive treatment (IPTp) with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine.

modules.name: Medical Disorders in Pregnancy: Thyroid, Liver (AFLP, ICP), Renal and Epilepsy

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 53 (Renal and Urinary Tract), Ch 55 (Hepatic, Biliary, and Pancreatic), Ch 58 (Endocrine), Ch 60 (Neurological)

mustKnow.fact: Overt maternal hypothyroidism (TSH >2.5 to 3.0 mIU/L with low free T4) impairs fetal neuropsychological development and elevates miscarriage risk, requiring immediate levothyroxine replacement.

Propylthiouracil (PTU) is preferred for hyperthyroidism in the first trimester due to lower teratogenicity, switching to methimazole in second/third trimesters to avoid PTU-induced severe maternal hepatotoxicity.

Acute fatty liver of pregnancy (AFLP) is a third-trimester emergency associated with fetal long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (LCHAD) deficiency, diagnosed by Swansea criteria (>=6 of 14 features).
AFLP carries high maternal-fetal mortality from microvesicular steatosis, profound hypoglycemia, coagulopathy, and renal failure, mandating prompt maternal stabilization and immediate delivery.

Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) presents with severe pruritus of palms and soles worse at night with elevated total serum bile acids; levels >=100 micromol/L carry high risk of sudden stillbirth.
Ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA at 10 to 15 mg/kg/day) is first-line therapy to alleviate pruritus and lower bile acids in ICP, with delivery planned at 36 to 37 weeks for bile acids >=100 micromol/L.
Labetalol, hydralazine, and methyldopa are safe antihypertensive agents for chronic kidney disease in pregnancy, while ACE inhibitors and ARBs remain strictly contraindicated.

Antiepileptic monotherapy at lowest effective dose with high-dose preconceptional folic acid (4 to 5 mg daily) minimizes major congenital malformation risks, with levetiracetam and lamotrigine having best safety profiles.

sections.name: Labour, Delivery, PPH, Operative Obstetrics and Puerperium

modules.name: Physiology and Mechanisms of Normal Labour, Partograph and Third Stage Management

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 21 (Physiology of Labor), Ch 22 (Normal Labor)

mustKnow.fact: Four phases of parturition comprise phase 1 (uterine quiescence and cervical softening), phase 2 (activation, myometrial oxytocin receptors increase 100-fold), phase 3 (active labour), and phase 4 (involution).
First stage of labour encompasses latent phase and active phase; contemporary ACOG/SMFM guidelines define active labour starting at 6 cm cervical dilatation.
mustKnow.source: Williams Obs 25e Ch 22; Zhang et al

mustKnow.fact: Cardinal movements of labour in vertex presentation follow strict sequence: engagement, descent, flexion, internal rotation, extension, restitution, external rotation, and expulsion.
Engagement occurs when the greatest transverse diameter of fetal head (biparietal diameter) passes through pelvic inlet, corresponding to station zero (ischial spines) on vaginal examination.
WHO modified partograph initiates recording at 4 cm dilatation in active phase, featuring an Alert line (1 cm/hr rate of cervical dilatation) and an Action line drawn 4 hours parallel to right.

Cervical dilatation crossing to the right of the Action line indicates protracted or arrested labour progress, mandating obstetric reassessment for cephalopelvic disproportion and augmentation or cesarean delivery.

Active management of third stage of labour (AMTSL) reduces postpartum haemorrhage by 60 percent, comprising prophylactic uterotonic (oxytocin 10 IU IM), controlled cord traction (Brandt-Andrews maneuver), and uterine massage.
Delayed umbilical cord clamping for 1 to 3 minutes in vigorous term and preterm infants increases neonatal iron stores and reduces intraventricular hemorrhage and necrotizing enterocolitis.

modules.name: Fetal Malpresentations: Breech, Face, Brow, Shoulder Dystocia and Cord Prolapse

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 23 (Abnormal Labor), Ch 27 (Vaginal Delivery), Ch 28 (Breech Delivery)

mustKnow.fact: Breech presentations comprise frank breech (hips flexed, knees extended, 65 percent), complete breech (hips and knees flexed, 25 percent), and incomplete or footling breech (one or both feet prolapsed, 10 percent).
External cephalic version (ECV) is offered from 36 to 37 weeks in uncomplicated singleton breech, achieving overall success rates of 50 to 60 percent.
Assisted vaginal breech delivery maneuvers include Pinard maneuver for footling, Lovset maneuver for extended arms, and Mauriceau-Smellie-Veit maneuver or Piper forceps for the aftercoming head.

Face presentation with mento-posterior position cannot deliver vaginally because the fetal brow is impacted behind pubic symphysis, requiring cesarean delivery unless spontaneous rotation to mento-anterior occurs.
Shoulder dystocia is an obstetric emergency where the anterior fetal shoulder impacts behind pubic symphysis, diagnosed by the 'turtle sign' (fetal head retracting tightly against perineum).
Primary maneuvers for shoulder dystocia are McRoberts maneuver (hyperflexion and abduction of maternal thighs) and concurrent suprapubic pressure (Rubin I), resolving over 50 percent of cases.

Secondary maneuvers for refractory shoulder dystocia include internal rotational maneuvers (Woods screw, Rubin II), delivery of posterior arm, and as last resort Zavanelli cephalic replacement for emergency cesarean.

Umbilical cord prolapse presents with palpable pulsating loop in vagina after rupture of membranes, managed by digital elevation of presenting part, steep Trendelenburg or knee-chest position, and immediate cesarean delivery.

modules.name: Induction and Augmentation of Labour: Bishop Score, Dinoprostone, Misoprostol and Oxytocin

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 26 (Induction and Augmentation of Labor)

mustKnow.fact: Modified Bishop score assesses cervical readiness across 5 components (dilatation, effacement, station, consistency, position); a score >=8 predicts successful vaginal delivery similar to spontaneous labour, while <=5 indicates an unripe cervix.

Mechanical cervical ripening methods include Foley balloon catheter (inflated with 30 to 50 mL sterile water) or Cook double balloon, preferred in women with prior cesarean delivery to avoid uterine rupture.
Prostaglandin E2 (dinoprostone) is available as intracervical gel (0.5 mg) or sustained-release vaginal insert (10 mg over 24 hours), withheld when regular contractions begin.
Prostaglandin E1 analogue (misoprostol) is administered orally (25 micrograms 2-hourly) or vaginally (25 micrograms 4-hourly) for cervical ripening in unscarred uteri.
Prostaglandins (misoprostol and dinoprostone) are strictly contraindicated for cervical ripening in women with a previous uterine scar due to significantly heightened uterine rupture risk.

Oxytocin infusion is initiated at low dose (1 to 2 mU/min) and titrated by 1 to 2 mU/min every 30 minutes until an adequate contraction pattern is established (3 to 4 contractions per 10 minutes lasting 40 to 60 seconds).

Uterine tachysystole is defined as more than 5 contractions in a 10-minute window averaged over 30 minutes, managed by reducing or stopping oxytocin, maternal lateral repositioning, and subcutaneous terbutaline.
Artificial rupture of membranes (amniotomy) combined with oxytocin shortens interval to delivery in active labour but is avoided with unengaged fetal head to prevent cord prolapse.

modules.name: Postpartum Haemorrhage: Atony, Balloon Tamponade, Compression Sutures, Embolisation and Transfusion

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 41 (Obstetrical Hemorrhage)

mustKnow.fact: Postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) is clinically defined as cumulative blood loss >=1000 mL or blood loss accompanied by signs or symptoms of hypovolemia within 24 hours postpartum regardless of route of delivery.

The 4Ts framework categorizes PPH etiologies into Tone (uterine atony, 70 to 80 percent), Trauma (lacerations, rupture, inversion, 20 percent), Tissue (retained placenta/membranes, 10 percent), and Thrombin (coagulopathies, 1 percent).

First-line medical uterotonics for atonic PPH include oxytocin (10 to 40 IU IV infusion), methylergonovine (0.2 mg IM, contraindicated in hypertension), carboprost tromethamine (PGF2-alpha, 0.25 mg IM, contraindicated in asthma), and misoprostol (800 micrograms sublingually).

Tranexamic acid (1 g IV over 10 minutes within 3 hours of birth, repeatable after 30 minutes if bleeding continues) significantly reduces death due to bleeding without increasing thromboembolic events.
mustKnow.source: Williams Obs 25e Ch 41; WOMAN Trial Lancet

mustKnow.fact: Intrauterine balloon tamponade (Bakri balloon inflated with 300 to 500 mL sterile saline) controls refractory atonic haemorrhage and provides a tamponade test before proceeding to laparotomy.

Surgical uterine compression sutures include the B-Lynch brace suture, Hayman vertical sutures, and Cho square sutures, which compress the anterior and posterior uterine walls to tamponade the placental bed.

Stepwise surgical devascularization incorporates bilateral uterine artery ligation (O'Leary stitches), utero-ovarian vessel ligation, and internal iliac (hypogastric) artery anterior division ligation.

Massive transfusion protocol in severe obstetric haemorrhage utilizes a balanced 1:1:1 ratio of packed red blood cells, fresh frozen plasma, and platelets, keeping fibrinogen above 200 mg/dL with cryoprecipitate.

modules.name: Operative Vaginal Delivery (Forceps, Vacuum), Caesarean Delivery and Peripartum Hysterectomy

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 29 (Operative Vaginal Delivery), Ch 30 (Cesarean Delivery and Peripartum Hysterectomy), Ch 31 (Prior Cesarean Delivery)

mustKnow.fact: Prerequisites for operative vaginal delivery comprise fully dilated cervix, ruptured membranes, engaged fetal head, known cephalic presentation and position, emptied maternal bladder, and adequate analgesia.

ACOG/RCOG classifies operative vaginal delivery by station: outlet (scalp visible without separating labia, fetal skull at pelvic floor), low (leading bony point at station +2 or lower), and midpelvic (station 0 to +1).

Simpson forceps with elongated cephalic curve are used for molded fetal heads, Elliott forceps with rounder curve for unmolded heads, and Kielland forceps with minimal pelvic curve and sliding lock for deep transverse arrest rotation.
Vacuum extraction cup placement must be centered precisely over the flexion point on the sagittal suture (3 cm anterior to posterior fontanelle) to promote flexion, descent, and autorotation.

Transverse lower uterine segment incision (Kerr incision) is standard for cesarean section, offering low blood loss and low rupture risk (<0.5 to 1.0%) in subsequent pregnancies compared to classical vertical incision (4 to 9%).
Trial of labour after cesarean (TOLAC) with one prior low transverse scar achieves 60 to 80 percent success rate, while prostaglandins are avoided for induction due to heightened rupture risk.

Emergency peripartum hysterectomy is indicated for unmanageable life-threatening postpartum haemorrhage refractory to medical and conservative surgical interventions, most commonly from placenta accreta spectrum or uterine rupture.

Subtotal (supracervical) hysterectomy is faster with less ureteral and bladder dissection in hemodynamically unstable patients, unless lower uterine segment or cervical placenta accreta necessitates total hysterectomy.

modules.name: Puerperal Complications: Puerperal Sepsis, Mastitis, VTE and Postpartum Depression

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 36 (The Puerperium), Ch 37 (Puerperal Complications), Ch 52 (Thromboembolic Disorders), Ch 61 (Psychiatric Disorders)

mustKnow.fact: Puerperal pyrexia is defined as temperature of 38.0 C (100.4 F) or higher on any 2 of the first 10 days postpartum, exclusive of the first 24 hours.

Puerperal endometritis is the commonest cause of postpartum fever, characteristically polymicrobial (aerobic and anaerobic vaginal flora), treated with intravenous clindamycin (900 mg 8-hourly) and gentamicin (5 mg/kg daily).

Septic pelvic thrombophlebitis (SPT) involves infected thrombus in ovarian veins or deep pelvic veins, presenting as persistent fever spiking despite broad-spectrum antibiotics, resolving with therapeutic low-molecular-weight heparin.
Puerperal mastitis is most frequently caused by Staphylococcus aureus entering through nipple fissures, managed with continued breastfeeding or milk expression and oral flucloxacillin or cephalexin.
Fluctuant breast mass refractory to antibiotics indicates breast abscess, requiring ultrasound-guided percutaneous needle aspiration or surgical incision and drainage.

Venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk is 20- to 80-fold higher in the first 6 weeks postpartum than in non-pregnant women, with deep vein thrombosis occurring predominantly (80 percent) in left lower extremity iliofemoral veins.
Postpartum blues affects up to 70 to 80 percent of women, peaking around postpartum days 4 to 5 and resolving spontaneously within 10 to 14 days without pharmacotherapy.

Postpartum psychosis occurs in 1 to 2 per 1000 births, presenting with acute confusion, paranoia, mania, and delusions of infant harm, constituting an emergency mandating immediate psychiatric inpatient admission.

modules.name: Maternal Mortality Ratio, Near-Miss Obstetric Events and Safe Motherhood Initiatives

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 1 (Overview), Ch 46 (General Considerations), Ch 47 (Critical Care and Trauma); WHO Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Maternal mortality ratio (MMR) is the number of maternal deaths during pregnancy or within 42 days of pregnancy termination per 100,000 live births, regardless of duration and site of pregnancy.

Direct obstetric deaths result from obstetric complications of the pregnant state (haemorrhage, preeclampsia, sepsis, obstructed labour, unsafe abortion), accounting for 70 to 75 percent of global maternal deaths.
Indirect obstetric deaths result from previously existing disease or disease developing during pregnancy aggravated by physiological effects (cardiac disease, viral hepatitis, malaria, tuberculosis).

WHO maternal near-miss (MNM) is defined as a woman who survived life-threatening obstetric conditions (organ dysfunction criteria including cardiovascular shock, respiratory intubation, renal dialysis, or hysterectomy).
mustKnow.source: WHO Near-Miss Approach; Williams Obs 25e Ch 47

mustKnow.fact: The Three Delays model identifies contributors to maternal mortality: delay in deciding to seek care (Phase 1), delay in reaching an appropriate obstetric facility (Phase 2), and delay in receiving adequate emergency care at facility (Phase 3).
mustKnow.source: Thaddeus and Maine; Williams Obs 25e Ch 1

mustKnow.fact: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) and Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) under National Health Mission provide direct cash transfers and free entitlements (drugs, diagnostics, diet, transport, C-section) to eliminate out-of-pocket costs.
mustKnow.source: MoHFW Guidelines India; Williams Obs 25e Ch 1

mustKnow.fact: LaQshya initiative focuses on improving quality of care in labor rooms and maternity operation theatres to reduce maternal and newborn mortality and eliminate mistreatment of women in labor.
Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3.1 targets reducing global maternal mortality ratio to less than 70 per 100,000 live births by the year 2030.

modules.name: Obstetrics and Gynaecology High-Yield Mixed Review

topics.book: Williams Obstetrics 25e; Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e

mustKnow.fact: Menopausal hormone replacement therapy with estrogen increases bone mineral density and significantly reduces hip fractures, but combined estrogen-progestin therapy after 5 years elevates invasive breast cancer and venous thromboembolism risks.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 8; WHI Trial

mustKnow.fact: Amniotic fluid lecithin-to-sphingomyelin (L/S) ratio exceeding 2.0 indicates mature fetal surfactant production and low risk of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome.

Periconceptional folic acid supplementation is 400 micrograms daily for primary prevention of neural tube defects, and 4000 micrograms (4 mg) daily starting 1 month before conception for secondary prevention in women with prior affected birth.

In gestational diabetes 50 g one-hour glucose challenge screening test, plasma glucose level exceeding 140 mg/dL identifies high risk warranting definitive diagnostic 100 g or 75 g oral glucose tolerance testing.
The standard diagnostic triad of congenital toxoplasmosis comprises chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, and diffuse intracranial calcifications.

Uterine inversion during third stage of labour presents with neurogenic shock and haemorrhage, managed by immediate manual replacement (Johnson maneuver) before placental removal and uterine relaxation with halogenated anaesthetics or nitroglycerin.
Human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes 16 and 18 account for over 70 percent of invasive cervical carcinomas, producing oncogenic proteins E6 (binding p53) and E7 (binding retinoblastoma pRb protein).

Mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst) is the most frequent benign germ cell ovarian neoplasm in young women, with 1 to 2 percent undergoing malignant transformation predominantly into squamous cell carcinoma.

sections.name: Gynaecological Anatomy, Endocrinology, Infertility and Contraception

modules.name: Embryology of the Urogenital System, Müllerian Anomalies and Pelvic Anatomy

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 1 (Development and anatomy of female sexual organs and pelvis)

mustKnow.fact: Paramesonephric (Müllerian) ducts develop laterally to mesonephric ducts, with their cranial non-fused portions forming the fallopian tubes and caudal fused portions forming the uterovaginal canal (uterus, cervix, upper two-thirds of vagina).
Lower one-third of the vagina derives from the paired endodermal sinovaginal bulbs of the urogenital sinus, joining the Müllerian tubercle to establish vaginal patency.
Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome represents 46,XX congenital absence of the uterus and upper vagina with normal ovarian function and female secondary sexual characteristics.
Uterine septum (Class V ASRM) is the commonest structural Müllerian anomaly, resulting from incomplete resorption of the midline septum between fused Müllerian ducts, treated hysteroscopically.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 1; ASRM Classification

mustKnow.fact: Uterine artery arises from the anterior division of the internal iliac artery and crosses anterior and superior to the ureter ('water under the bridge') 1.5 to 2.0 cm lateral to the supravaginal cervix.

The three most vulnerable anatomical sites for ureteral injury during pelvic gynaecological surgery are at the pelvic brim (infundibulopelvic ligament), lateral cervix (uterine artery crossing), and anterolateral vaginal fornix.

Primary pelvic organ support relies on the levator ani muscle complex (pubococcygeus, puborectalis, iliococcygeus) and Level I DeLancey suspensory condensations (cardinal-uterosacral ligament complex).

Lymphatic drainage of the cervix and lower uterine body passes laterally to obturator, internal iliac, and external iliac lymph nodes, while the uterine fundus drains via ovarian vessels directly to para-aortic nodes.

modules.name: Neuroendocrine Regulation of Menstrual Cycle and Steroidogenesis

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 3 (Hormonal control of the menstrual cycle and hormonal disorders)

mustKnow.fact: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) is secreted in pulsatile fashion from the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus, with high-frequency pulses favoring LH secretion and low-frequency pulses favoring FSH secretion.

Two-cell, two-gonadotropin theory dictates that theca interna cells under LH stimulation synthesize androgens (androstenedione and testosterone) from cholesterol, while granulosa cells under FSH stimulation express aromatase (CYP19A1) to convert androgens into estrogens.
FSH stimulates early follicular growth and recruitment; rising estradiol from the dominant follicle exerts negative feedback on FSH, leading to atresia of non-dominant follicles.
Mid-cycle LH surge is triggered by sustained positive estradiol feedback exceeding 200 pg/mL for at least 36 to 48 hours, inducing resumption of oocyte meiosis I and follicle rupture.
Ovulation occurs consistently 34 to 36 hours after the onset of the LH surge, or approximately 10 to 12 hours after the peak of the surge.
The luteal phase has a fixed physiological lifespan of 14 plus or minus 2 days, maintained by corpus luteum secretion of progesterone and estradiol.
Endometrial histology demonstrates subnuclear glycogen vacuoles appearing 36 to 48 hours after ovulation (cycle day 16 to 17), representing the earliest morphological hallmark of progesterone action.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 3; Noyes criteria

mustKnow.fact: Luteolysis occurs in the absence of beta-hCG, precipitating sharp drops in progesterone and estradiol that induce spiral arteriolar spasm, lysosomal enzyme release, and menstruation.

modules.name: Primary and Secondary Amenorrhoea: Hypothalamic, Pituitary, Ovarian and Outflow Tract

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 3 (Hormonal control of the menstrual cycle and hormonal disorders)

mustKnow.fact: Primary amenorrhoea is defined as absence of menses by age 13 in the absence of secondary sexual characteristics, or by age 15 in the presence of normal secondary sexual development.
Turner syndrome (45,XO) is the commonest genetic cause of primary amenorrhoea, featuring hypergonadotropic hypogonadism, streak gonads, short stature, coarctation of aorta, and bicuspid aortic valve.

Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome presents with primary amenorrhoea and normal female thelarche (breast development) with absent uterus and blind-ending vagina, differentiated from androgen insensitivity by female testosterone levels and 46,XX karyotype.

Complete androgen insensitivity syndrome (CAIS, 46,XY) features absent androgen receptors, presenting with female external genitalia, scant pubic/axillary hair, male testosterone levels, and cryptorchid testes requiring post-pubertal gonadectomy.
Kallmann syndrome is hypogonadotropic hypogonadism caused by deficient GnRH neuronal migration from olfactory placode, characterized by anosmia and prepubertal gonadotropin levels.
Secondary amenorrhoea is defined as cessation of menses for 3 months in previously regular cycles or 6 months in previously irregular cycles, with pregnancy being the commonest cause.
Asherman syndrome consists of intrauterine synechiae and endometrial destruction following post-abortal or postpartum curettage or genital tuberculosis, confirmed and lysed via hysteroscopy.
Progesterone challenge test (medroxyprogesterone acetate 10 mg daily for 10 days) evaluates endogenous estrogen priming; withdrawal bleeding confirms anovulation with intact outflow tract.

modules.name: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Rotterdam Criteria, Hyperandrogenism and Metabolic Management

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 3 (Hormonal control of the menstrual cycle and hormonal disorders)

mustKnow.fact: Rotterdam 2003 criteria require at least two of three features for PCOS diagnosis: oligo- or anovulation, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound, after excluding mimickers.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 3; Rotterdam Consensus

mustKnow.fact: Polycystic ovarian morphology on high-frequency ultrasound is defined by 20 or more follicles measuring 2 to 9 mm in either ovary, or an ovarian volume exceeding 10 mL.
mustKnow.source: International PCOS Guidelines 2023; Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 3

mustKnow.fact: Modified Ferriman-Gallwey (mFG) visual scoring assesses terminal hair growth across 9 body areas; a score of 4 to 8 or greater defines clinical hirsutism depending on ethnic population.
Pathophysiology features elevated LH-to-FSH ratio (>2:1 to 3:1), thecal androgen hypersecretion, compensatory hyperinsulinemia that suppresses hepatic SHBG, and elevated free circulating androgens.

First-line ovulation induction agent for anovulatory infertility in women with PCOS is letrozole (aromatase inhibitor, 2.5 mg to 7.5 mg daily for 5 days), achieving superior live birth and ovulation rates compared to clomiphene.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 3, 7; PPCOS II Trial

mustKnow.fact: Combined oral contraceptive pills containing anti-androgenic progestins (cyproterone acetate or drospirenone) are first-line pharmacotherapy for menstrual irregularity, acne, and hirsutism in women not seeking pregnancy.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 3; International Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Late-onset 21-hydroxylase deficiency congenital adrenal hyperplasia is excluded in hirsute women by demonstrating morning follicular phase 17-hydroxyprogesterone below 2 ng/mL (6 nmol/L).

Unchecked chronic anovulatory estrogen exposure without cyclical progesterone opposition confers a 3- to 4-fold increased lifetime risk of endometrial hyperplasia and type I endometrial adenocarcinoma.

modules.name: Abnormal Uterine Bleeding: FIGO PALM-COEIN Classification and Management

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 4 (Disorders of menstrual bleeding); FIGO 2011/2018

mustKnow.fact: FIGO PALM-COEIN classification categorizes non-gestational abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) in reproductive years into structural causes (Polyp, Adenomyosis, Leiomyoma, Malignancy/hyperplasia) and non-structural causes (Coagulopathy, Ovulatory dysfunction, Endometrial, Iatrogenic, Not otherwise classified).

Normal menstrual cycle parameters are frequency 24 to 38 days, duration up to 8 days, cycle-to-cycle variation under 7 to 9 days, and subjective blood loss that does not interfere with daily quality of life.

Endometrial biopsy is mandatory in women presenting with AUB aged 45 years or older, or under 45 with risk factors for endometrial cancer (obesity, chronic anovulation, tamoxifen, Lynch syndrome, failed medical therapy).

Saline infusion sonohysterography (SIS) and diagnostic hysteroscopy provide superior sensitivity over routine pelvic ultrasound for differentiating focal intracavitary lesions (endometrial polyps and submucosal fibroids).

Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS 52 mg) provides up to 90 percent reduction in menstrual blood loss, representing first-line medical therapy for heavy menstrual bleeding without structural cavity distortion.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 4; NICE Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Non-hormonal medical options taken during menses comprise tranexamic acid (antifibrinolytic, 1 g orally 3 times daily, 50% reduction) and mefenamic acid (NSAID inhibiting endometrial prostaglandins, 30% reduction).

Acute severe abnormal uterine bleeding is managed by intravenous tranexamic acid, high-dose intravenous conjugated equine estrogen or high-dose oral progestins, or intrauterine Foley balloon tamponade.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 4; ACOG Committee

mustKnow.fact: Second-generation endometrial ablation (thermal balloon, radiofrequency, or cryotherapy) is a minimally invasive surgical alternative to hysterectomy in women with completed childbearing.

modules.name: Precocious and Delayed Puberty, Perimenopause, POI and Menopausal Hormone Therapy

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 3 (Hormonal control), Ch 8 (Menopause and post-reproductive health)

mustKnow.fact: Precocious puberty is development of secondary sexual characteristics before age 8 in girls, classified as central (GnRH-dependent, elevated LH) or peripheral (GnRH-independent, autonomous ovarian/adrenal steroid production).

McCune-Albright syndrome is peripheral precocious puberty caused by somatic activating GNAS gene mutations, featuring the triad of café-au-lait spots with jagged 'coast of Maine' borders, polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, and autonomous ovarian cysts.
Delayed puberty is absence of breast development by age 13 or absence of menarche by age 15, investigated with bone age radiography, basal gonadotropins, and karyotyping.
Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) is amenorrhoea for 4 or more months before age 40, confirmed by elevated serum FSH exceeding 25 to 40 IU/L on two occasions 4 weeks apart.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 8; ESHRE Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Women with POI require hormone replacement therapy continued at least until the average age of natural menopause (age 51) to preserve bone mineral density and reduce cardiovascular mortality.
Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) with systemic estrogen requires opposed progestogen in women with an intact uterus to prevent endometrial hyperplasia and adenocarcinoma.
The 'window of opportunity' concept dictates that initiating MHT within 10 years of menopause or before age 60 yields favorable cardiovascular risk-benefit ratio and slows osteoporotic bone loss.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 8; IMS Consensus

mustKnow.fact: Transdermal estradiol avoids hepatic first-pass metabolism, conferring lower risks of venous thromboembolism and stroke compared to oral estrogen regimens, favored in obese women or those with thrombotic risk factors.

modules.name: Evaluation of Infertility, Tubal Patency, Ovarian Reserve, Ovulation Induction and ART

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 7 (Subfertility)

mustKnow.fact: Infertility is defined as failure to achieve clinical pregnancy after 12 months of regular unprotected sexual intercourse (or after 6 months in women aged 35 years or older).

WHO 2021 manual semen analysis lower reference limits comprise volume >=1.4 mL, sperm concentration >=16 million/mL, total motility >=42 percent (progressive motility >=30 percent), and normal forms >=4 percent.
mustKnow.source: WHO Laboratory Manual 6th Ed 2021; Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 7

mustKnow.fact: Ovarian reserve testing utilizes serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH, <1.1 ng/mL indicates poor reserve) and transvaginal ultrasound antral follicle count (AFC <5 to 7 indicates diminished reserve).
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 7; Bologna criteria

mustKnow.fact: Mid-luteal serum progesterone measured on cycle day 21 (7 days before expected menses in a 28-day cycle) exceeding 30 nmol/L (10 ng/mL) confirms ovulatory cycle.
Hysterosalpingography (HSG) evaluates tubal patency and uterine cavity contours via fluoroscopic radiopaque contrast injection during early follicular phase, with spill demonstrating tubal patency.
Diagnostic laparoscopy and chromopertubation with methylene blue dye is the gold standard investigation for tubal patency and peritoneal endometriosis.

Intrauterine insemination (IUI) is indicated for mild male factor subfertility, cervical factor, and unexplained subfertility provided at least one fallopian tube is patent and total motile sperm count exceeds 5 to 10 million.
Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) is a dangerous complication of gonadotropin stimulation driven by VEGF, preventable by GnRH agonist trigger instead of hCG and freeze-all embryo transfer.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 7; ESHRE Guidelines

modules.name: Contraceptive Modalities: MEC Criteria, Hormonal, IUCD, Emergency and Surgical Sterilisation

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 6 (Contraception and abortion); WHO MEC 5th Edition

mustKnow.fact: WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC) classifies contraceptive safety into Category 1 (unrestricted use), Category 2 (advantages outweigh risks), Category 3 (risks outweigh advantages), and Category 4 (unacceptable health risk, absolute contraindication).
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 6; WHO MEC 5e

mustKnow.fact: Combined hormonal contraceptives are WHO MEC Category 4 in women aged 35 years or older smoking >=15 cigarettes daily, hypertension >=160/100 mmHg, history of DVT/PE, migraine with aura, and active breast cancer.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 6; WHO MEC

mustKnow.fact: Etonogestrel subdermal single-rod implant (Nexplanon 68 mg) is the most effective reversible contraceptive method (failure rate <0.05%), functioning for 3 to 5 years via ovulation suppression.

Depot medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA, 150 mg IM every 12 weeks) provides effective contraception but causes reversible bone mineral density loss and delayed return to fertility averaging 9 to 10 months.

Copper intrauterine device (Cu-IUCD 380A) is effective for 10 to 12 years by inducing sterile cytotoxic inflammatory reaction in the endometrial cavity that inhibits sperm transport and fertilization.
Copper IUCD inserted within 5 days (120 hours) of unprotected intercourse is the most effective emergency contraceptive method, reducing pregnancy risk by over 99 percent.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 6; WHO Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Oral emergency contraception options include ulipristal acetate (selective progesterone receptor modulator, 30 mg single dose up to 120 hours) and levonorgestrel (1.5 mg single dose within 72 hours).

Female surgical sterilisation via Pomeroy laparoscopic tubal ligation or bipolar coagulation carries an overall lifetime failure rate of approximately 0.5 percent (1 in 200), with ectopic pregnancy accounting for one-third of post-sterilisation failures.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 6; CREST Study

sections.name: Benign Gynaecology, Infections, Urogynaecology and Gynaecological Oncology

modules.name: Vaginal Discharge Syndromes: Bacterial Vaginosis, Trichomoniasis, Candidiasis and Genital Ulcers

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 9 (Sexually transmitted infections and related conditions); CDC STI Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Bacterial vaginosis is diagnosed by Amsel criteria (at least 3 of 4: thin homogenous discharge, vaginal pH >4.5, positive amine whiff test with 10% KOH, clue cells on wet mount >20%).
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 9; CDC Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Nugent score is the laboratory gold standard for bacterial vaginosis, scoring Gram stain morphotypes from 0 to 10 based on loss of Lactobacillus and replacement by Gardnerella and Mobiluncus.

Trichomoniasis caused by flagellated protozoan Trichomonas vaginalis presents with copious frothy yellow-green malodorous discharge, punctate cervical colpitis macularis ('strawberry cervix'), and motile trichomonads on saline wet mount.
First-line therapy for both bacterial vaginosis and trichomoniasis is oral metronidazole, with mandatory simultaneous partner treatment for trichomoniasis.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 9; CDC Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Vulvovaginal candidiasis presents with thick white curd-like ('cottage cheese') discharge, severe pruritus vulvae, normal vaginal pH (<4.5), and budding pseudohyphae on 10% KOH preparation.

Genital herpes simplex virus (HSV-2 predominantly) presents with painful, grouped vesicles on an erythematous base that unroof into shallow ulcers with tender inguinal lymphadenopathy, diagnosed by viral PCR.

Syphilis presents in primary stage with a single painless indurated ulcer (chancre) and non-tender rubbery lymphadenopathy, screened by non-treponemal tests (VDRL/RPR) and confirmed by treponemal assays (TPHA/FTA-ABS).
Chancroid caused by Haemophilus ducreyi produces painful, non-indurated soft ulcers with ragged undermined edges and suppurative inguinal bubo formation.

modules.name: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease, Tubo-Ovarian Abscess and Female Genital Tuberculosis

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 9 (Sexually transmitted infections and related conditions)

mustKnow.fact: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) is ascending polymicrobial infection from endocervix, most commonly initiated by Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae followed by endogenous anaerobes.

CDC minimum clinical diagnostic criteria for empiric PID treatment in sexually active women comprise lower abdominal or pelvic pain plus cervical motion tenderness, uterine tenderness, or adnexal tenderness on bimanual examination.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 9; CDC PID Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Outpatient empiric antibiotic regimen for mild-to-moderate PID combines single-dose intramuscular ceftriaxone (500 mg) plus oral doxycycline (100 mg twice daily) and oral metronidazole (500 mg twice daily) for 14 days.

Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome (perihepatitis) presents with right upper quadrant pleuritic pain from violin-string fibrinous adhesions between anterior liver capsule and abdominal wall following chlamydial or gonococcal PID.

Tubo-ovarian abscess (TOA) is an inflammatory adnexal mass requiring inpatient intravenous antibiotics (cefotetan/cefoxitin plus doxycycline, or clindamycin plus gentamicin) and image-guided percutaneous drainage if refractory.
Female genital tuberculosis results from secondary hematogenous spread from pulmonary focus, with the fallopian tubes involved in 90 to 100 percent of cases and endometrium in 50 to 60 percent.
Genital tuberculosis classic triad presents with infertility, menstrual disturbances (oligomenorrhoea/amenorrhoea from endometrial scarring), and chronic pelvic pain.
Hysterosalpingography in genital tuberculosis exhibits classic signs: lead pipe rigid tube, tobacco pouch appearance of fimbria, rosary bead calcifications, and golf club ampulla.

modules.name: Uterine Leiomyomas: FIGO Classification, Medical Therapy, Myomectomy and Uterine Artery Embolisation

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 12 (Benign conditions of the uterus, cervix and endometrium); FIGO 2011/2018

mustKnow.fact: FIGO fibroid classification system categorizes leiomyomas from Type 0 (pedunculated intracavitary) through Type 1 to 2 (submucosal), Type 3 to 5 (intramural/subserosal), Type 6 to 7 (subserosal), and Type 8 (parasitic/cervical).
Uterine fibroids are monoclonal estrogen- and progesterone-dependent smooth muscle neoplasms exhibiting cytogenetic mutations in MED12 (70 percent of cases) and HMGA2.
Red (carneous) degeneration occurs predominantly during pregnancy or puerperium due to rapid growth exceeding blood supply with subsequent venous thrombosis and hemorrhagic infarction.

Medical therapy to reduce fibroid size and treat heavy bleeding prior to surgery includes GnRH agonists (leuprolide), oral GnRH antagonists (relugolix, elagolix with add-back therapy), and selective progesterone receptor modulators.
Hysteroscopic myomectomy is the procedure of choice for symptomatic FIGO Type 0 and Type 1 submucosal fibroids measuring up to 4 to 5 cm in diameter.
Abdominal or laparoscopic myomectomy requires multilayer myometrial closure to minimize postoperative uterine rupture risk during subsequent pregnancy.

Uterine artery embolisation (UAE) utilizes polyvinyl alcohol particles injected into bilateral uterine arteries, achieving 50 to 60 percent fibroid volume reduction but carrying risks of post-embolisation syndrome and ovarian insufficiency.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 12; REST trial

mustKnow.fact: Leiomyosarcoma is a rare malignant differential (<0.5 percent) characterized by tumor necrosis, cytologic atypia, and mitotic index >=10 per 10 high-power fields, not arising from pre-existing benign leiomyomas.

modules.name: Endometriosis and Adenomyosis: Pathogenesis, Deep Infiltrating Endometriosis and Stepped Care

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 11 (Benign conditions of ovary and pelvis), Ch 12 (Benign conditions of uterus)

mustKnow.fact: Endometriosis is defined by functional endometrial glands and stroma outside the uterine cavity, explained primarily by Sampson retrograde menstruation theory with peritoneal implantation and neuroangiogenesis.
The classic symptom complex features secondary dysmenorrhoea, deep dyspareunia, dyschezia, dysuria, and subfertility, with pain severity poorly correlating with revised ASRM surgical stage.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 11; ESHRE Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Ovarian endometrioma ('chocolate cyst') contains thick altered dark blood, exhibiting diffuse low-level homogeneous ground-glass echoes without internal vascularity on pelvic ultrasound.

Laparoscopic cystectomy with excision of the endometrioma pseudocapsule is superior to simple fenestration and ablation for relieving pain and reducing recurrence, though careful technique is required to protect ovarian reserve.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 11; Cochrane Review

mustKnow.fact: Deep infiltrating endometriosis (DIE) penetrates more than 5 mm beneath peritoneal surface, commonly involving uterosacral ligaments, pouch of Douglas, rectovaginal septum, and bowel muscularis.

First-line medical therapy for endometriosis-associated pain includes continuous combined oral contraceptives, high-dose progestins (dienogest 2 mg daily), or the levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS).
Adenomyosis is presence of heterotopic endometrial glands and stroma deep within myometrium (>=2.5 mm from junctional zone) with surrounding smooth muscle hyperplasia.
MRI findings diagnostic of adenomyosis demonstrate asymmetric thickening of the junctional zone exceeding 12 mm and punctate high-signal myometrial islands on T2-weighted imaging.

modules.name: Benign Adnexal Masses, Mature Teratoma, Endometrioma and Ovarian Torsion Emergency

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 11 (Benign conditions of the ovary and pelvis)

mustKnow.fact: Functional ovarian cysts (follicular cysts and corpus luteum cysts) represent exaggerated physiological cycle variants, thin-walled and unilocular, typically resolving spontaneously within 2 to 3 menstrual cycles.
Corpus luteum cyst rupture typically presents during secretory phase (cycle day 20 to 26) with acute pelvic pain and hemoperitoneum, mimicking ruptured ectopic pregnancy.

Mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst) derives from all three germ cell layers, exhibiting Rokitansky protuberance, fat-fluid levels, and acoustic shadow from dense calcified elements (teeth, hair, sebum).

Serous cystadenoma is thin-walled unilocular filled with clear watery fluid (lined by ciliated tubal-type epithelium), whereas mucinous cystadenoma is multilocular and massive, lined by tall columnar mucin-secreting epithelium.

Ovarian torsion is an acute surgical emergency caused by twisting of the ovary and fallopian tube on its infundibulopelvic and utero-ovarian vascular pedicle, obstructing venous return followed by arterial compromise.

Doppler ultrasound demonstrating enlarged heterogeneous ovary with peripheralized follicles and absent or dampened venous and arterial flow supports torsion, though presence of arterial flow does not exclude early torsion.
Emergency laparoscopic detorsion with ovarian preservation and cystectomy is the modern standard of care regardless of macroscopic dusky or congested appearance in premenopausal women.
Risk of Malignancy Index (RMI 1) combines ultrasound score (U), menopausal status (M), and serum CA-125 level (RMI = U x M x CA-125); an RMI score >200 carries 75 percent sensitivity for malignancy.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 11; Jacobs et al

modules.name: Pelvic Organ Prolapse, POP-Q Staging, Urinary Incontinence and Urogenital Fistulae

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 10 (Urogynaecology and pelvic floor problems)

mustKnow.fact: Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification (POP-Q) system measures 9 specific anatomical landmarks in centimeters relative to the hymen (plane 0), staging prolapse from Stage 0 (no prolapse) to Stage IV (complete eversion / procidentia).
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 10; ICS POP-Q

mustKnow.fact: Anterior compartment prolapse includes cystocele and cystourethrocele (points Aa and Ba), apical prolapse encompasses uterine descent or vaginal vault prolapse (points C and D), and posterior compartment includes rectocele and enterocele (points Ap and Bp).

First-line conservative management for symptomatic pelvic organ prolapse comprises pelvic floor muscle training (Kegel exercises) and vaginal supportive or space-occupying pessaries (ring or Gellhorn pessary).
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 10; NICE Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Abdominal or laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy using synthetic polypropylene mesh anchored to anterior longitudinal sacral ligament is the gold standard surgical repair for apical vaginal vault prolapse.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 10; Cochrane Review

mustKnow.fact: Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) is involuntary leakage on effort or exertion (sneezing, coughing) caused by urethral hypermobility or intrinsic sphincter deficiency without detrusor contraction.
Mid-urethral sling procedures (retropubic TVT or transobturator TOT) provide effective dynamic urethral support for stress incontinence refractory to pelvic muscle rehabilitation.

Urge urinary incontinence caused by involuntary detrusor overactivity is treated primarily with bladder training and anticholinergics (solifenacin, oxybutynin) or beta-3 adrenergic agonist mirabegron.

Vesicovaginal fistula (VVF) in developing regions arises predominantly from prolonged obstructed labour leading to ischemic necrosis, presenting with continuous unremitting involuntary urinary drainage.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 10; WHO Fistula Guide

modules.name: Gynaecological Procedures: Laparoscopy, Hysteroscopy, Colposcopy and Endometrial Sampling
