topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 2 (Gynaecological examination), Ch 17 (Gynaecological surgery and therapeutics)

mustKnow.fact: Primary laparoscopic entry via Veress needle or open Hasson cut-down at umbilical ring requires establishing pneumoperitoneum with carbon dioxide up to an intra-abdominal pressure of 12 to 15 mmHg.

Palmer point in the left upper quadrant (3 cm below left subcostal margin in midclavicular line) is the safe alternative laparoscopic entry site in patients with suspected periumbilical adhesions or prior laparotomies.
Diagnostic hysteroscopy utilizes normal saline distension fluid for bipolar electrosurgical systems to avoid glycine-induced dilutional hyponatremia and fluid overload.
Fluid deficit monitoring during operative hysteroscopy mandates procedure cessation when deficit reaches 1000 mL for hypotonic electrolyte-free media or 2500 mL for isotonic normal saline.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 17; AAGL Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Colposcopic evaluation applies 3 to 5 percent dilute acetic acid to visualize acetowhite changes and abnormal vascular patterns (punctation and mosaicism) within the transformation zone.

Lugol iodine solution (Schiller test) stains glycogen-rich normal squamous epithelium dark mahogany brown, whereas dysplastic or malignant areas lacking glycogen remain unstained (Schiller-positive mustard yellow).
Outpatient manual endometrial aspiration biopsy with Pipelle cannula achieves diagnostic sensitivity exceeding 95 percent for detecting endometrial carcinoma in postmenopausal bleeding.
Cervical cone biopsy or loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) provides diagnostic and therapeutic excision of CIN 2 to 3, requiring negative endocervical and ectocervical margins.

modules.name: Cervical Cancer Screening, Colposcopy, Bethesda System, FIGO Staging and Radical Hysterectomy

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 16 (Premalignant and malignant disease of the lower genital tract); FIGO 2018

mustKnow.fact: High-risk HPV testing every 5 years between ages 25 and 65 is the preferred cervical screening strategy, offering superior sensitivity over liquid-based cytology for preventing high-grade CIN and invasive cancer.

Bethesda System reporting stratifies epithelial cytology into atypical squamous cells (ASC-US, ASC-H), low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL, representing HPV/CIN 1), and high-grade SIL (HSIL, representing CIN 2/3).

FIGO 2018 staging allows cross-sectional imaging (MRI, CT, PET-CT) and pathological findings to assign stage, incorporating lymph node metastases as Stage IIIC (IIIC1 pelvic, IIIC2 para-aortic nodes).
Stage IA1 microinvasive cervical carcinoma with stromal invasion depth under 3 mm without lymphovascular space invasion is managed conservatively with cervical conization.
Early invasive cervical cancer (Stage IB1, IB2, IIA1) is treated with Type C radical hysterectomy (Wertheim-Meigs operation) with bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy.
Open radical abdominal hysterectomy achieves superior progression-free and overall survival compared to minimally invasive laparoscopy or robotic surgery in early cervical cancer.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 16; LACC Trial NEJM 2018

mustKnow.fact: Locally advanced cervical cancer (Stage IB3, IIA2, IIB, III, IVA) is definitively managed with concurrent chemoradiation combining weekly cisplatin with external beam radiation and high-dose-rate brachytherapy.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 16; NCCN Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Fertility-sparing radical trachelectomy with pelvic lymphadenectomy is indicated in young women desiring childbearing with tumor size <=2 cm (Stage IA2 to IB1) and negative pelvic nodes.

modules.name: Endometrial Carcinoma: Bokhman Dual Pathways, FIGO Staging and Molecular ProMisE Classification

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 15 (Malignant disease of the uterus); FIGO 2023

mustKnow.fact: Bokhman dual model distinguishes Type I estrogen-dependent endometrioid adenocarcinoma arising from atypical hyperplasia with PTEN and KRAS mutations from Type II non-estrogen serous carcinoma arising in atrophic endometrium with p53 mutations.

Postmenopausal bleeding carries a 10 percent probability of underlying endometrial carcinoma, mandating transvaginal ultrasound; an endometrial thickness <=4 mm confers a negative predictive value >99 percent.
Lynch syndrome (hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer from germline DNA mismatch repair gene mutations MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2) carries a 40 to 60 percent lifetime risk of endometrial cancer.

FIGO 2023 staging incorporates molecular classification: POLE ultramutated (favorable prognosis), MMR-deficient (intermediate), p53 abnormal (poor prognosis), and NSMP (no specific molecular profile).
Stage I endometrial cancer is confined to uterine corpus: Stage IA involves <50% myometrial invasion, and Stage IB involves >=50% myometrial invasion.
Standard primary surgical management is total laparoscopic or abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (TLH/BSO) and sentinel lymph node mapping.

Sentinel lymph node mapping using cervical injection of indocyanine green (ICG) with near-infrared fluorescence accurately detects pelvic nodal metastasis while avoiding lymphedema from complete lymphadenectomy.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 15; FIRES Trial

mustKnow.fact: Adjuvant vaginal brachytherapy provides excellent local cuff control with low rectal-urinary toxicity in intermediate-risk Stage I disease, whereas high-risk or advanced disease receives external beam radiation and carboplatin-paclitaxel chemotherapy.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 15; PORTEC trials

modules.name: Epithelial Ovarian Malignancies, Germ Cell, Sex Cord-Stromal Tumours and Cytoreductive Surgery

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 14 (Malignant disease of the ovary); FIGO 2014

mustKnow.fact: High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC) represents 70 percent of epithelial ovarian cancers, predominantly originating from serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC) lesions in the distal fimbriated fallopian tube with universal TP53 mutations.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 14; Kurman model

mustKnow.fact: BRCA1 and BRCA2 germline mutations confer 40 to 60 percent and 15 to 25 percent lifetime risks of ovarian cancer respectively, managed with risk-reducing bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (RRBSO) by age 35 to 40 (BRCA1) or 40 to 45 (BRCA2).

Ovarian cancer stages surgically: Stage I confined to ovaries, Stage II pelvic extension below pelvic brim, Stage III peritoneal implants outside pelvis or retroperitoneal lymph nodes, and Stage IV distant metastases (pleural effusion with positive cytology, parenchymal liver/splenic metastases).

Primary cytoreductive (debulking) surgery aims for complete cytoreduction with zero residual macroscopic disease (R0), the single most significant independent modifiable prognostic determinant of survival.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 14; Bristow meta-analysis

mustKnow.fact: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy with 3 cycles of carboplatin and paclitaxel followed by interval debulking surgery is non-inferior to primary surgery in advanced disease with extensive non-resectable peritoneal carcinomatosis.

PARP inhibitors (olaparib, niraparib) provide major progression-free survival benefit as maintenance therapy in advanced BRCA-mutated or homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) ovarian cancers responding to platinum.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 14; SOLO-1 Trial

mustKnow.fact: Malignant germ cell tumors (dysgerminoma, endodermal sinus yolk sac tumor, immature teratoma) predominantly affect young women, treated with fertility-sparing unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and BEP chemotherapy (bleomycin, etoposide, cisplatin).

Granulosa cell tumor is a sex cord-stromal neoplasm characterized by Call-Exner bodies, elevated serum inhibin-B, and hyperestrogenism causing endometrial hyperplasia, notable for late recurrences beyond 10 to 20 years.

modules.name: Premalignant and Malignant Lesions of the Vulva and Vagina, Paget Disease and Radical Vulvectomy

topics.book: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 13 (Benign conditions of vulva and vagina), Ch 16 (Premalignant and malignant disease); FIGO 2021

mustKnow.fact: Vulval squamous intraepithelial neoplasia divides into usual-type VIN (HPV-associated, HPV 16/18, seen in younger women) and differentiated VIN (dVIN, HPV-negative, associated with lichen sclerosus and TP53 mutations in elderly women with high progression rate).
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 16; ISSVD Classification

mustKnow.fact: Lichen sclerosus is a chronic lymphocytic inflammatory dermatosis presenting with severe intractable pruritus vulvae, porcelain-white atrophic patches, loss of vulval architecture ('figure-of-eight' distribution), and phimosis of clitoral hood.
Superpotent topical corticosteroids (clobetasol propionate 0.05% ointment) represent first-line treatment for vulval lichen sclerosus, reducing pruritus and risk of progression to squamous carcinoma.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 13; BASHH Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Extramammary Paget disease of the vulva presents as an erythematous, velvety, eczematoid weeping plaque with white porcelain islands ('strawberries and cream' appearance), characterized microscopically by large mucin-positive Paget cells.
Vulval carcinoma (over 90 percent squamous cell carcinoma) stages by FIGO 2021 based on tumor size, depth of invasion (>1 mm is invasive), and groin lymph node metastasis status.

Stage IB vulval carcinoma (tumor size >2 cm or stromal invasion depth >1 mm with negative nodes) is managed by radical local wide local excision with 1 cm clinical margins and inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy.

Sentinel lymph node biopsy using technetium-99m radiocolloid and blue dye is safe in unifocal vulval tumors <4 cm with clinically negative groins, substantially reducing lower limb lymphedema morbidity.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 16; GROINSS-V I/II

mustKnow.fact: Clear cell adenocarcinoma of the vagina and cervix in young daughters is historically linked to in-utero maternal exposure to diethylstilbestrol (DES) taken in early pregnancy.
mustKnow.source: Ten Teachers Gynae 21e Ch 16; Herbst et al
